2027-06-10.title: Thursday of the third week after Pentecost
readings: Epaphroditus came close to death for the work of Christ: honor such people
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth
2027-06-10.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Third Sunday after Pentecost.
2027-06-10.verse: When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth
theo: St Paul's letters are full of names we pass over quickly, and today the Church stops at one of them. Epaphroditus was a member of the little church at Philippi, sent by them to Paul in prison with a gift and with orders to stay and help him. In prison he fell ill, so ill that he nearly died, and when he recovered he was homesick and worried that his people were anxious about him. So Paul sends him home with a letter, and with a testimonial that any of us would treasure: “Still, I think it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and co-worker and fellow soldier, your messenger and minister to my need.” Brother, co-worker, fellow soldier: three titles of friendship, labour and struggle. And the word translated “messenger” is the Greek word apostolos: the Philippians had sent him, and he was their apostle to Paul. The Church in her season of Pentecost remembers that the apostolic mission does not belong only to the Twelve; it is carried on by thousands of people whose names never reach a history book.

Paul asks the Philippians for something important: “Welcome him then in the Lord with all joy, and honor such people, because he came close to death for the work of Christ, risking his life to make up for those services that you could not give me.” Honour such people. Every parish is held up by an Epaphroditus or two: the catechism teacher who has given thirty Sunday mornings a year for twenty years, the sacristan who opens the church before dawn, the woman who sits with the sick when no one else will go, the young people who carry chairs and clean the hall. In these first weeks of June, when the schools of Kerala reopen in the monsoon rain, we might think also of teachers, bus drivers and cooks in school kitchens who will spend themselves for our children all year. And we may think of the many nurses from our parishes who serve in hospitals far from home, like Epaphroditus, sometimes at real risk to their health. Paul also says something tender: “God had mercy on him, and not only on him but on me also, so that I would not have one sorrow after another.” The great apostle does not pretend to be beyond grief; he thanks God for sparing his friend. St John Chrysostom remarks that Paul is not ashamed to show that he was anxious and would have mourned, because love for the brethren is no weakness in a saint (Homilies on Philippians 9, in substance).

The Gospel takes us back to the Last Supper: “I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth.” Jesus is a patient teacher. He does not pour everything into the disciples at once; he knows what they can carry. The Spirit continues his teaching through the whole life of the Church, leading her deeper into the one truth that Jesus is, not adding a new Gospel but opening up the one Gospel: “he will take what is mine and declare it to you.” This is what happens in the councils of the Church, in the prayer of the saints, in the slow growth of a believer's understanding over a lifetime. It happens to each of us too. There are things in our faith we could not bear at fifteen and understand at fifty; there are crosses whose meaning we will see only later. Like a good teacher at the start of a school year, the Spirit begins where we are. Our part is to stay in the classroom: to keep coming to the Holy Qurbono, where the word is read and the Bread of Life is given, and to let him guide us, one step at a time, into all the truth.
outline: Ask: whom have I never thanked for the hidden service that keeps my parish and my family going?
Epaphroditus, the Philippians' apostle to Paul, and the unnamed bearers of the mission.
The parish workers, teachers and nurses who spend themselves for others; God's mercy in sickness.
The patient teaching of the Spirit, who takes what is Christ's and declares it.
“When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth.”
live: Write a note, send a message or say a word of thanks this week to one person whose hidden service holds up your parish, school or family.
Choose one question about the faith that troubles you, bring it to prayer before the Holy Qurbono, and ask the Spirit to teach you in his time.
2027-06-10.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you sent your apostles and their co-workers to carry the Gospel, and you send your Spirit of truth to guide your Church into all the truth. We thank you for every Epaphroditus among us, for those who serve without being noticed, for teachers and catechists, for nurses and carers, for those who risk their health for others. Have mercy on them in sickness, as you had mercy on your servant, and spare them one sorrow after another. Teach us patiently, as we are able to bear it, and lead us one step at a time into the fullness of your truth. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The Spirit who guides the Church into all the truth takes what is Christ's and gives it to us: at the altar he makes bread and wine the Body and Blood of the Lord, and makes us one body of brothers, co-workers and fellow soldiers.

quick: Paul sends back to Philippi Epaphroditus, his brother, co-worker and fellow soldier, who nearly died in the service of Christ.
Paul asks the church to welcome him with joy and to honour such people.
Jesus promises that the Spirit of truth will guide the disciples into all the truth, taking what is his and declaring it to them.
2027-06-10.action: Thank one person today whose hidden work makes your life easier.
2027-06-10.question: Which truth of faith is the Spirit patiently teaching me now, that I could not bear before?

family.explain: St Paul had a helper called Epaphroditus. He worked so hard for Jesus that he became very sick and nearly died. But God made him well again. Paul told the church: welcome him with joy and honour people like him. In every family and parish there are people who work hard and quietly for others. This week schools open again; teachers, drivers and cooks will work hard for children all year.
family.intention: We pray for teachers and all who serve children in schools, and for nurses and carers who look after the sick.
family.ask: Ask: “Who works quietly for our family, and how can we say thank you to that person this week?”

illus: In a parish in Kollam district, the parish council once decided to honour its oldest catechism teacher on the day she retired. When they counted the years, they found that she had taught on Sunday mornings for forty-one years, and that three of the priests now serving in the eparchy had been in her class. She was embarrassed by the fuss and said she had done nothing special. One of the priests stood up and said: Teacher, when I was nine and my father was in the Gulf and my mother was ill, you were the one who noticed that I had not eaten breakfast. You gave me your own lunch. I have forgotten most of the catechism you taught me that year, but I have never forgotten that. Every parish has people like her.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit of truth, guide us into all the truth, and teach us to honour all who labour among us for the work of Christ. Amen.
share: My brother and co-worker and fellow soldier (Philippians 2:25). Who has been a co-worker in Christ to me?
Welcome him then in the Lord with all joy, and honor such people (Philippians 2:29). Whom have I failed to honour?
I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now (John 16:12). What is the Spirit teaching me slowly?
interc: For the Church, that the Holy Spirit may keep guiding her into all the truth, in fidelity to the apostles.
For catechists, sacristans, choir members and all hidden workers in our parishes.
For teachers, students and school staff at the start of the new school year, and for safety on the roads in the monsoon.
For nurses, doctors and carers, especially those from our parishes who serve far from home.
For the sick, that God may have mercy on them as he had mercy on Epaphroditus.
pm.close: Father, you raise up co-workers for the Gospel in every generation, and you send your Spirit to lead your Church into all the truth. Bless all who serve in hidden ways, heal those who are sick, and keep us faithful learners of your truth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today St Paul introduces us to a man most of us hardly know: Epaphroditus. Paul calls him my brother and co-worker and fellow soldier, your messenger and minister to my need (Philippians 2:25). The Philippians had sent him to help Paul in prison, and he became so ill that he nearly died.

Paul says: Welcome him then in the Lord with all joy, and honor such people (Philippians 2:29). Every parish is held up by people like Epaphroditus, catechists, sacristans, those who care for the sick, those who clean and arrange. This month the schools reopen, and many teachers and staff will work hard for our children. Let us honour such people, and thank them.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth (John 16:12–13). The Holy Spirit is a patient teacher. He teaches the Church through the centuries, and he teaches each of us through our lives, step by step.

So let us stay in his school. Let us keep coming to the Holy Qurbono, keep reading the word, keep praying, even when we do not understand everything. And let us be co-workers like Epaphroditus, giving ourselves for the work of Christ without asking for honour. Amen.
kids: Children, schools are opening again! Your teachers will help you learn new things, a little at a time. Jesus said that the Holy Spirit is like a teacher too: he helps us understand God a little more every day. Today we also heard about Epaphroditus, a helper of St Paul who worked so hard that he became sick. St Paul said: honour people like him. Who helps you every day? Your parents, your teachers, your bus driver? Say thank you to them this week!

intro: Theme: “When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth.”
On Thursday of the third week after Pentecost: Epaphroditus, the co-worker who nearly died for Christ, the honour due to hidden servants, and the patient teaching of the Spirit.

sub: The mission carried by unnamed hands.
q: Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to do it.
esteem them very highly in love because of their work.
points.apply: Thank, by name and in person, one hidden worker of your parish this Sunday.

sub: Sickness in the service of Christ.
Paul is not ashamed of his anxiety.
Mercy spares us one sorrow after another.
q: The Lord sustains them on their sickbed; in their illness you heal all their infirmities.
the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our affliction
points.apply: Visit or call one person who is sick, especially a health worker who has fallen ill.

sub: The Spirit takes what is Christ's.
q: All your children shall be taught by the Lord, and great shall be the prosperity of your children.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit each day this week before you or your children begin study or work.

concl: The apostolic mission is carried by many Epaphroditus figures, and the Church must honour them.
The Spirit of truth teaches patiently, taking what is Christ's and giving it to us as we can bear it.
2027-06-10.resolve: Honour those who serve in hidden ways, and stay faithfully in the school of the Holy Spirit.
